output.review_comment:
Fixes 1 and 2 look correct and match the docstring. Periods now count started 30-day periods ("days 1-30 are the first period"), and `+ 5000` before `// 10000` rounds halves up.

Fix 3 has to be reverted. The docstring (the stated source of truth) says "The cap always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee", which means `min(max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS), balance_cents // 5)`. The new branch applies the cap only when the raw fee is above it. When fee < cap < minimum it returns the minimum, which is above the documented cap. The PR description admits this logic was added only to make `test_small_balance_pays_minimum` pass (`late_fee_cents(1800, 45) == 500`); under the docstring the answer is 360. The inline comment "cap always wins (even below minimum)" is also misleading, because the code doesn't do that. For small balances this can overcharge customers beyond the documented cap.

Please restore `return min(max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS), balance_cents // 5)` and raise the test/docstring conflict with the requester, so they can decide whether the test or the docstring is wrong. Don't encode the test's expectation in the implementation.
